text.text_excerpt: This is a cute little neighborhood coffee joint with a clean, modern feel. I live a few blocks away and like to pop in now and then whenever I have a latte craving. There is normally just one person behind the counter so if there is a line it takes a hot minute to get what you came for. The staff is always pleasant and there is a nice assortment of light breakfast and lunch items. My only qualm is that they seem to disregard your milk request as I've twice asked for 2% or whole and was given skim (by two different employees). If you're looking for a Starbucks replacement, Cafe Treme may not be your scene. I personally love the small community feel of this vibrantly-painted gem in the midd...

I don't love every cafe, but I really do love this little spot. It's perfect. It's comfortable, and it's menu is appropriate as are the prices. And it reinvents an old corner cottage likely from the mid 19th century. Whenever I'm in Treme and I have a little time to kill, I make it a point to stop in and sit a spell.

We were strolling through the neighborhood looking for a rumored piece of Banksy street art (found it at the corner of St. Ann & Villere on the side of some old slave quarters.) It was a hot and muggy afternoon in NOLA yesterday and we needed a cold drink, and Cafe Treme appeared to us like an oasis. We got a bottle of Sprite, which hit the spot, and couldn't resist ordering a slice of the amazing looking coconut cake in the display case. The cafe was clean, comfortably air conditioned, the staff was very friendly, and the coconut cake was out of this world.
